motto: Serving Greywater Falls since 1887, and the lake somewhat longer.
weather: Overcast, 40°F, a thin fog sitting on the lake till nearly ten

undercurrent.phenomenon: The name has crossed from ledger to daylight congregation to standing patron; the town's remaining work is letting the routine hold without needing further proof, one ordinary Monday at a time.
undercurrent.note: Peak beat resolved cleanly: Sarah Voss's file closes as an ordinary loan rather than an occasion, which is the season's real crest, the town choosing paperwork over ceremony. Continuing the scheduled ease toward coda by day 26-28. Remaining threads to close gently: Russ's folded riddle (still unopened, may stay that way as his resolution), Toby's near-blank notebook (due a small closing beat, maybe the one entry that isn't a refusal), the sixth cup as settled ordinary practice. Agnes holding her declared silence. Doreen, Gerald, Hank essentially closed. Wren's dual witness role now easing into simple stewardship of a joint ledger. No new escalation warranted; hold level in the low 50s through mid-arc-close, dropping further as coda nears.

editor.name: Wren Aldercott
editor.voice: Dry, precise, allergic to drama, which is unfortunate given recent events. Writes like a person holding a clipboard while standing in rising water. Lets one true thing slip per edition, usually in the last line.

season_arc.premise: Calloway finishes reshelving the east alcove in the last cataloguer's 2009 order and finds, tucked behind where the ninth book sat, a library card checked out that same interrupted Wednesday and never returned. It is due back today. The borrower's name is nobody currently living in Greywater Falls has ever heard of, and the little pocket calendar stamped inside has fourteen years of due-date stamps on it already, one for every year since, each in a different hand.
